welcome_page.title: Car – Travel choices and safety
welcome_page.description:
A few questions about getting around by car. If you rarely travel by car, we only ask why.

Taking part is voluntary and you can skip any question. Your answers are not linked to your name, and no public authority receives them.

Learn more about SmartUrbanity

Only the SmartUrbanity research team reads your answers. We keep them for research for 36 months; then we delete them or make them anonymous.

questionnaire.title: Car – Travel choices and safety

questions.text: Do you travel by car at least once a week?
questions.help: As the driver or as a passenger, also car sharing.

questions.text: Why do you rarely travel by car? (Select all that apply)

options.text: I don't have a car or a driving licence
It costs too much (fuel, parking, tolls, insurance)
Traffic and finding a parking space take too long
Driving is stressful or tiring for me
I feel unsafe on the road by car
I prefer other ways of getting around, for example for the environment

questions.text: In the same trip, do you usually combine the car with another way of travelling?
questions.help: For example bike and train, or car and metro. A short walk to a stop or to a parked vehicle does not count.

questions.text: Which other ways of travelling do you use in the same trip? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Walking (as the main mode for most of the trip, not short access or transfer walking)
Taxi or similar service (e.g. Uber, Bolt)

questions.text: What difficulties do you experience when combining different transport modes (e.g. bike + public transport, car + metro, walking + bus)?

options.text: Vehicles are too crowded (e.g. no space for a bicycle or luggage)
Poor coordination between modes (long waiting times, missed connections)
Lack of infrastructure (e.g. no bicycle parking or no bicycle access on public transport)
Complicated transfers (stations far apart, unclear routes)
Cost is too high when combining modes
Services are infrequent or do not run in the evening
Physical effort is too high (e.g. carrying a bicycle or walking long distances)
I do not experience significant difficulties

questions.text: When you face these difficulties, how do you mostly respond?

options.text: I stop using one of the modes (e.g. stop bringing my bike)
I switch to a single mode (e.g. only car, only public transport)
I change the time of travel (e.g. avoid peak hours)
I change the route or transfer point
I choose a different combination of modes
I continue using the same combination despite difficulties
I reduce how often I make that trip
I look for alternative solutions (e.g. bike sharing instead of own bike)
I avoid that trip entirely if possible
I do not experience significant difficulties

sections.title: Car – When the car is hard to replace

questions.text: Select the uses that apply to you. For each selected use, tell us how often and what would let you leave the car. If none apply, select None of these.

columns.label: What would let you leave the car for this?

options.label: More frequent and reliable public transport, also in the evening
An accompanied or on-demand transport service

sections.title: Car – Other ways to get around

questions.text: What would help you choose an alternative to the car for some of your trips?

options.text: More frequent and reliable public transport, also in the evening
Knowing it's better for the environment
I need the car for my situation (e.g., disability, children, loads, work shifts)
Routes and vehicles that are accessible for my disability or health condition
Nothing: the car suits my trips
Not for me: I can't walk or cycle far (e.g. health, age, carrying things)

questions.text: If you could use a shared bike or e-scooter for free, would you try it?

options.text: Not for me: I can't ride one

questions.text: If driving cost more (fuel, parking, tolls), would you use the car less?

options.text: No, I'd use it the same
I'd stop using it for most trips
I could not reduce it: I have no alternative
Not for me: I don't pay these costs (e.g. company car, passenger)

questions.text: Do you think about pollution from vehicles when you choose how to travel?
questions.help: Pollution means exhaust fumes and gases that harm the air and the climate.

options.text: No, it doesn't affect my choices
I think about it now and then
It often affects how I travel
I try to use the car less because of it

questions.text: When you drive, how confident are you that you can avoid a crash when someone appears suddenly?
questions.help: For example a pedestrian stepping out, a cyclist or scooter cutting across you, or a car door opening.

questions.text: When you travel by car, who on the road makes you feel unsafe? (Select all that apply)
questions.help: Think of specific behaviour, such as passing too close or not giving way, rather than everyone in a group.

questions.text: When you travel by car, which of these situations make you feel unsafe? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Unsafe behaviour from drivers, riders or pedestrians
Lack of safe or adequate roads, junctions, signs or lighting
